\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मोची} (mochī)}{मोची (mochī)}]{\mw{मोची} (mochī) — a cobbler}

\label{lesson:MW-C265-mochi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a potter, then the Marwadi for a carpenter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मोची}}
\textbf{\mw{मोची}} — \emph{mochī} — \textquotedblleft{}a cobbler\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{मोची} \mw{जूती} \mw{सीवै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mochī jūtī sīvai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cobbler stitches a shoe.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{मोची}} (\emph{mochī}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{mocika}, \textquotedblleft{}tanner and cobbler\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL takes from an Iranian word for a shoe. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry; it lists Hindi \emph{mocī} (CDIAL 10349).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mochī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mochī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mochī jūtī sīvai hai.} — The cobbler stitches a shoe.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a potter, then the Marwadi for a carpenter, then say \emph{mochī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{मोची} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cobbler\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मूंडणो} (mū̃ḍṇo)}{मूंडणो (mū̃ḍṇo)}]{\mw{मूंडणो} (mū̃ḍṇo) — to shave}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Married Into the Family to Shoes, Shaves and Shirts}

\label{lesson:MW-R265-review-260-265}



\begin{quote}
Say the Marwadi for a daughter-in-law and a son-in-law.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a daughter-in-law, a son-in-law, a brother's wife, a sister's husband, a wife's brother
  \item a mother's sister, a brother's son, a sister's son, a son's son, a daughter's son
  \item a person (when counting), a travelling trader, a woman's friend, a village headman, a craftsman
  \item a temple priest, a gardener, an oil-presser, a washerman, a goldsmith
  \item to shape (metal or clay), a blacksmith, to hammer, a potter, a carpenter
  \item a cobbler, a barber, to shave, a tailor, a servant
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A daughter-in-law? (\textbf{\mw{बहू}}, \emph{bahū}.) A son-in-law? (\textbf{\mw{जंवाई}}, \emph{jãvāī}.) A brother's wife? (\textbf{\mw{भावज}}, \emph{bhāvaj}.) A sister's husband? (\textbf{\mw{बहनोई}}, \emph{bahnoī}.) A wife's brother? (\textbf{\mw{साळो}}, \emph{sāḷo}.) A mother's sister? (\textbf{\mw{मासी}}, \emph{māsī}.) A brother's son? (\textbf{\mw{भतीजो}}, \emph{bhatījo}.) A sister's son? (\textbf{\mw{भाणजो}}, \emph{bhāṇjo}.) A son's son? (\textbf{\mw{पोतो}}, \emph{poto}.) A daughter's son? (\textbf{\mw{दोहितो}}, \emph{dohito}.) A person (when counting)? (\textbf{\mw{जणो}}, \emph{jaṇo}.) A travelling trader? (\textbf{\mw{बणजारो}}, \emph{baṇjāro}.) A woman's friend? (\textbf{\mw{सहेली}}, \emph{sahelī}.) A village headman? (\textbf{\mw{चौधरी}}, \emph{chaudhrī}.) A craftsman? (\textbf{\mw{कारीगर}}, \emph{kārīgar}.) A temple priest? (\textbf{\mw{पुजारी}}, \emph{pujārī}.) A gardener? (\textbf{\mw{माळी}}, \emph{māḷī}.) An oil-presser? (\textbf{\mw{तेली}}, \emph{telī}.) A washerman? (\textbf{\mw{धोबी}}, \emph{dhobī}.) A goldsmith? (\textbf{\mw{सुनार}}, \emph{sunār}.) To shape (metal or clay)? (\textbf{\mw{घड़णो}}, \emph{ghaṛṇo}.) A blacksmith? (\textbf{\mw{लुहार}}, \emph{luhār}.) To hammer? (\textbf{\mw{ठोकणो}}, \emph{ṭhokṇo}.) A potter? (\textbf{\mw{कुम्हार}}, \emph{kumhār}.) A carpenter? (\textbf{\mw{सुथार}}, \emph{suthār}.) A cobbler? (\textbf{\mw{मोची}}, \emph{mochī}.) A barber? (\textbf{\mw{नाई}}, \emph{nāī}.) To shave? (\textbf{\mw{मूंडणो}}, \emph{mū̃ḍṇo}.) A tailor? (\textbf{\mw{दरजी}}, \emph{darjī}.) A servant? (\textbf{\mw{चाकर}}, \emph{chākar}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
